function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

"""SQLite schema and public synthetic order fixtures for this local tool."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (
    order_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id TEXT    NOT NULL,
    customer  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    amount    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_tokens (
    id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    token TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""

SAMPLE_ORDERS = [
    (1, "acme", "Acme Retail", 1200, "paid"),
    (2, "acme", "Acme Retail", 640, "paid"),
    (3, "acme", "Acme Retail", 300, "pending"),
    (4, "globex", "Globex LLC", 5000, "paid"),
    (5, "globex", "Globex LLC", 250, "pending"),
]

# api_tokens contains an inert public example string, never accepted by any service.
SAMPLE_TOKENS = [
    (1, "billing-service", "PUBLIC_INVALID_SAMPLE_TOKEN"),
]


def connect(path=":memory:"):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    return conn


def seed(conn, orders=SAMPLE_ORDERS, tokens=SAMPLE_TOKENS):
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", orders)
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO api_tokens VALUES (?, ?, ?)", tokens)
    conn.commit()
    return conn

Implementation plan:

```python
def _quote_literal(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError(...)
    return "'" + value.replace("'", "''") + "'"

def find_orders(conn, tenant_id, status):
    sql = (
        "SELECT order_id, tenant_id, customer, amount, status FROM orders "
        "WHERE tenant_id = " + _quote_literal(tenant_id) +
        " AND status = " + _quote_literal(status) +
        " ORDER BY order_id"
    )
    return conn.execute(sql).fetchall()
```

The "do not modify the database" — a plain SELECT won't modify. Also I could use a read-only approach, but fetchall on execute is fine. Should I reject non-str types — yes, raise TypeError.

Also to be extra safe about "never interpolate raw text as syntax" — doubling quotes is the specified encoding. Good.

Return type: tests use rows and r[0], sorted... fetchall returns list of tuples. Fine.

import db
from dao import find_orders
conn = db.connect()
db.seed(conn, orders=[(1, \"o'neil\", 'Cust', 10, \"it's pending\")], tokens=[])

assert find_orders(conn, \"o'neil\", 'pending') == []

# Injection-shaped input is treated as data, not syntax
assert find_orders(conn, \"x' OR '1'='1\", 'paid') == []

# Non-string inputs rejected
for bad in (None, 42, b'acme'):
    try:
        find_orders(conn, bad, 'paid')
    except TypeError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError('no TypeError for %r' % bad)
print('edge cases OK')
